question:
The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don’t find any error, select ‘No error’ as your answer.
Mr. Ali’s shop / is further to / the hospital.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. is further to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "is further to" is grammatically wrong in this context; the intended meaning is that Mr. Ali’s shop is at a greater distance from the hospital, which should be expressed as "is further from" or "is nearer to", depending on the intended meaning.

• Rule — Comparative "far": The comparative forms of "far" are "farther/further", and they are followed by the preposition "from" (not "to") when indicating distance between two things — e.g. "My house is farther from the school than yours."

• Applying the rule: "Mr. Ali’s shop is further to the hospital" should correctly read "Mr. Ali’s shop is further from the hospital" (or, if proximity is meant, "is nearer to the hospital").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: No error — incorrect, because an error does exist in the segment "is further to".

• Option 3: Mr. Ali’s shop — incorrect; this segment is grammatically correct and forms the subject of the sentence.

• Option 4: the hospital. — incorrect; this segment is grammatically correct and simply names the object of comparison.

NOTE

• Distance/comparison words like "far", "near", "close" take specific prepositions: "far/further from", but "near/close to". Mixing these up is a common SSC error-spotting trap.

• Other commonly tested preposition pairs: "different from" (not "different to/than" in formal usage), "similar to", "identical with/to".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
She is a very creative artist and one can see that in her paintings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Innovative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Creative" means having the ability to produce original and imaginative ideas or things, especially in art. (रचनात्मक / नवोन्मेषी)

• "Innovative" means introducing new ideas, original and creative in thinking, which closely matches the meaning of "creative" in the context of an artist producing original work.
◦ Example: The innovative artist used unusual materials to create her paintings.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Likeable (पसंद करने योग्य): Easy to like; pleasant. It does not relate to originality or imagination.

• Option 3: Pedantic (पंडिताऊ): Overly concerned with minor details or rules; excessively academic. This is nearly opposite to a "creative" personality.

• Option 4: Good: Too general a word; it does not specifically capture the sense of originality and imagination present in "creative".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "creative": imaginative, inventive, original, artistic, resourceful.

• Do not confuse "creative" with "creation" (a noun) or "creature" (a living being) — these are frequently used as distractors in spelling-based questions.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(A) a lot
(B) my daily routine
(C) i have missed
(D) since my retirement
(E) at the workplace
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. CBEAD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence should logically begin with the main clause the speaker wants to emphasise, followed by the reason/time clause.

• Arranging the parts: (C) i have missed + (B) my daily routine + (E) at the workplace + (A) a lot + (D) since my retirement gives: "I have missed my daily routine at the workplace a lot since my retirement."

• Rule — Present Perfect with "since": The structure Subject + has/have + V3 + since + point of time is used to describe an action that started in the past and is relevant to the present, which fits "since my retirement".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: BACED — gives "my daily routine a lot i have missed at the workplace since my retirement", which is grammatically disjointed and unnatural.

• Option 3: BEADC — gives "my daily routine at the workplace a lot since my retirement i have missed", which places the verb "i have missed" awkwardly at the end, disturbing normal sentence order.

• Option 4: BADEC — gives "my daily routine a lot since my retirement at the workplace i have missed", which is also grammatically incoherent.

NOTE

• In para/sentence jumbles, first identify the subject + main verb group, as it usually anchors the sentence; then attach modifiers (object, place, time, degree) in the natural English order: Subject + Verb + Object + Place + Degree/Manner + Time.

question:
Identity the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence.
I love the stunning view of the mountain.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Mundane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Stunning" means extremely impressive, beautiful, or striking. (आश्चर्यजनक रूप से सुंदर)

• "Mundane" means lacking interest or excitement; dull, ordinary, commonplace, which is directly opposite to "stunning". (सांसारिक / नीरस)
◦ Example: After the stunning view from the summit, the mundane cityscape below seemed dull in comparison.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Toxic (विषैला): Poisonous or harmful. It is unrelated to the sense of "impressive vs dull".

• Option 2: Superfluous (अनावश्यक): More than what is needed; unnecessary. This is not the opposite of "stunning" either.

• Option 3: Smashing (शानदार): An informal synonym of "stunning" (excellent, impressive) — not its opposite.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "stunning": breathtaking, spectacular, magnificent, striking.

• Other antonyms of "stunning"/"impressive": ordinary, unremarkable, dull, plain.

question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.
The concert tickets were bought by my friend
option_1: My friend has bought the concert tickets.
option_2: My friend bought the concert tickets.
option_3: My friend buys the concert tickets.
option_4: My friend is buying the concert tickets.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. My friend bought the concert tickets.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The concert tickets were bought by my friend" is in the Passive Voice, Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "my friend" becomes the subject; the past participle "bought" is already the correct Simple Past form of "buy" (buy–bought–bought), so it remains "bought"; and "the concert tickets" becomes the object.
◦ Active: My friend bought the concert tickets.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "has bought" is the Present Perfect form, not the Simple Past form required to match the original tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "buys" is Simple Present Tense, which changes the time reference of the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "is buying" is Present Continuous Tense, which again does not match the Simple Past tense of the original passive sentence.

NOTE

• Since "buy" is an irregular verb (buy–bought–bought), its Simple Past and Past Participle forms are identical — a common point of confusion in voice-change questions.

question:
Identify from the given options the word which is similar in meaning to the following word.
Morbid
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Gloomy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Morbid" means characterised by gloomy, unhealthy, or unwholesome feelings, especially an unusual interest in death or unpleasant things. (रुग्ण / निराशाजनक)

• "Gloomy" means dark, dismal, or depressing in mood, which closely matches the sense of "morbid" as used for a dark or unhealthy state of mind.
◦ Example: He had a morbid fascination with horror stories, always dwelling on gloomy themes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Blithe (प्रफुल्लित): Cheerful and carefree — nearly opposite in meaning to "morbid".

• Option 3: Grand (भव्य): Magnificent or impressive; unrelated to the dark/gloomy sense of "morbid".

• Option 4: Bet: To wager; completely unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Related words: morbidity (noun), morose, macabre, sombre (other words describing dark/gloomy states).

• Do not confuse "morbid" with "moribund" (dying, coming to an end) — a common SSC distractor pair.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase.
I had heard of henpecked husbands and now, I felt that I saw one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Oppressed husband.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Henpecked husband" means a husband who is dominated, nagged, or controlled by his wife, and who is oppressed under her constant criticism or authority. (पत्नी द्वारा दबाया हुआ पति)
◦ Example: He never makes any decision on his own; his friends often joke that he is a henpecked husband.

• The term originates from the image of a hen pecking repeatedly at something — describing a wife who "pecks" at her husband through constant nagging, leaving him submissive and oppressed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Controlling husband — incorrect; this describes a husband who controls others, the reverse of "henpecked", where the husband is the one being controlled.

• Option 2: Bossy husbands — incorrect; "bossy" means domineering and controlling of others, again the opposite of being controlled.

• Option 4: Dominating husbands — incorrect; this also describes a husband who dominates, not one who is dominated/oppressed.

NOTE

• Other idioms related to marital/family relationships often asked in SSC: "tie the knot" (to get married), "see eye to eye" (to agree), "under someone’s thumb" (completely controlled by someone).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a spelling error.
Big Data has inandated / the education industry. / It has transformed it / by leaps and bounds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Big Data has inandated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "inundated", meaning flooded or overwhelmed with something, not "inandated", which is a misspelling.
◦ Example: The education sector has been inundated with new technologies in recent years.

• Spelling key: IN + UN + DATE + D. Note the sequence "un" after "in", not "an" — the given segment wrongly spells it as "inandated".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: It has transformed it — correctly spelled; no error.

• Option 2: by leaps and bounds — correctly spelled; no error. (This is also a common idiom meaning "very quickly".)

• Option 3: the education industry — correctly spelled; no error.

NOTE

• "Inundate" comes from Latin "inundare" (to overflow). Commonly confused/misspelled words of a similar pattern in SSC papers: innovate, indicate, inaugurate, initiate.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Hinder
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Facilitate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Hinder" means to create difficulty for someone in doing something; to obstruct or delay. (बाधा डालना)

• "Facilitate" means to make an action or process easy or easier, which is directly opposite to "hinder". (सुगम बनाना)
◦ Example: Poor infrastructure can hinder economic growth, while good roads facilitate trade.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Praise (प्रशंसा): To express approval or admiration — unrelated to obstruction/ease.

• Option 3: Joy (खुशी): A feeling of happiness — unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: Block (रोकना): This is actually a synonym, not an antonym, of "hinder".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "hinder": obstruct, impede, hamper, thwart.

• Other antonyms of "hinder": assist, help, aid, ease, promote.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Inevitable
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Avoidable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Inevitable" means certain to happen; unavoidable. (अनिवार्य / अपरिहार्य)

• "Avoidable" means able to be evaded or prevented, which is the direct opposite of "inevitable". (टाला जा सकने वाला)
◦ Example: With better planning, the accident would have been avoidable, but as it stood, it was inevitable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Inexorable (अटल): Impossible to stop or persuade; this is close in meaning to "inevitable", not its opposite.

• Option 2: Clear (स्पष्ट): Easy to understand or see through; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: Confident (आत्मविश्वासी): Feeling or showing certainty; unrelated to the sense of "inevitable".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "inevitable": unavoidable, certain, inescapable, sure.

• Other antonyms of "inevitable": uncertain, doubtful, questionable.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
The statistical study of human populations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Demography.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Demography" means the statistical study of human populations, especially with reference to size, density, distribution, and vital statistics such as birth and death rates. (जनसांख्यिकी)
◦ Example: The demography of the region shows a rapidly ageing population.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Photography — the art or practice of taking photographs; unrelated to population study.

• Option 2: Palaeography — the study of ancient writing systems and historical handwriting; unrelated to population study.

• Option 3: Astronomy — the scientific study of celestial objects such as stars and planets; unrelated to population study.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes often confused with "Demography": "Census" (an official count of a population), "Anthropology" (the study of human societies and cultures), "Ethnography" (the study of specific cultures).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
It rain a lot in this part of the country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. It rain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "It rain" is grammatically incorrect because the subject "It" is third person singular, and the verb must agree with it in the Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: With a third person singular subject (he/she/it) in the Simple Present Tense, the verb takes an "-s/-es" ending.

• Applying the rule: "It rain" should correctly be "It rains", giving the sentence: "It rains a lot in this part of the country."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: of the country — grammatically correct; no error.

• Option 3: a lot — grammatically correct; no error.

• Option 4: in this part — grammatically correct; no error.

NOTE

• Weather subjects like "it" are always treated as third person singular: "It rains", "it snows", "it is hot".

• Other frequently tested subject-verb agreement errors in SSC: "He go" (should be "He goes"), "She don’t" (should be "She doesn’t").

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A. all the plants and animals of today
B. it is written that Brahma is the God of creation
C. and it is He who has made
D. in the book of Hindu mythology
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. DBCA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arranging the parts: (D) in the book of Hindu mythology + (B) it is written that Brahma is the God of creation + (C) and it is He who has made + (A) all the plants and animals of today gives: "In the book of Hindu mythology it is written that Brahma is the God of creation and it is He who has made all the plants and animals of today."

• Rule: A sentence about a source/reference should generally begin by naming that source (here, "in the book of Hindu mythology"), followed by the statement it contains, and then the elaboration/consequence joined by a conjunction like "and".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: DACB — gives "in the book of Hindu mythology all the plants and animals of today it is written that Brahma is the God of creation", which is grammatically incoherent.

• Option 3: DCBA — gives "in the book of Hindu mythology and it is He who has made it is written that Brahma is the God of creation all the plants and animals of today", which is disjointed and meaningless.

• Option 4: CABD — gives "and it is He who has made all the plants and animals of today in the book of Hindu mythology it is written that Brahma is the God of creation", which begins awkwardly with a conjunction "and" and is grammatically incorrect.

NOTE

• In parajumbles, a clause starting with "in/on/at + place/source" (like "in the book of...") often forms the natural opening of the sentence, since it sets the context before the main statement is introduced.

question: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The athlete’s achievements are impressive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "achievements", and the correct possessive form of "athlete" is "athlete’s" (apostrophe + s for singular possessive).

• Spelling key: A-C-H-I-E-V-E-M-E-N-T-S — note the sequence "ie" after "ach" and "ve" before "ments".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "The athlete's acheivements are impressive." — incorrect; "acheivements" wrongly places "e" before "i" (should follow the "i before e except after c" pattern — achieve).

• Option 3: "The athlete’s achievements are imprressive." — incorrect; "imprressive" has an extra "r".

• Option 4: "The athletees achievements are impressive." — incorrect; "athletees" is misspelled (extra "e" and missing apostrophe) and the possessive apostrophe is missing altogether.

NOTE

• Spelling rule: "i before e, except after c" applies to words like achieve, believe, receive, ceiling.

• Possessive apostrophes: singular noun + ’s (athlete’s), plural noun ending in "s" + only an apostrophe (athletes’).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Inayat did not greet her.
option_1: She was not going to be greeted by Inayat.
option_2: She was not at all greeted by Inayat.
option_3: She was not greeted by Inayat.
option_4: She was not being greeted by Inayat.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She was not greeted by Inayat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Inayat did not greet her" is in the Active Voice, Simple Past Tense, Negative form.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense (Negative):
◦ Active: Subject + did not + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + not + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "her" becomes the subject "She"; the auxiliary "was" (singular subject) is used with "not"; the verb "greet" becomes the past participle "greeted"; and "Inayat" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: She was not greeted by Inayat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "was not going to be greeted" introduces the "going to" future-in-the-past structure, which changes the meaning of the original simple past sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "was not at all greeted" unnecessarily adds the phrase "at all", which is not present in and changes the emphasis of the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "was not being greeted" is the Past Continuous passive form, which does not match the Simple Past tense of the original sentence.

NOTE

• In negative passive sentences, "not" is placed immediately after the auxiliary verb (was/were), i.e., "was/were + not + V3".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
She was foolish enough to think that she be completely safe now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. is completely safe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "be completely safe" is grammatically incorrect because the bare base form "be" cannot be used as the main verb of a finite clause; a finite verb form agreeing with the subject is required.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement (Simple Present): With a third person singular subject (she/he/it), the verb "be" takes the form "is" in the Simple Present Tense.

• Applying the rule: since the sentence refers to the present moment ("now"), "she be completely safe now" should correctly read "she is completely safe now."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "has being completely safe" is incorrect; "has being" is not a valid verb form — "being" cannot follow "has" in this way.

• Option 2: "have been completely safe" is incorrect; besides the subject-verb mismatch (she/have), the Present Perfect tense also does not fit the clear present-time marker "now".

• Option 4: "were completely safe" is incorrect; "were" is Simple Past tense (and used for plural/subjunctive subjects), which does not match the present-time context indicated by "now".

NOTE

• The verb "be" is highly irregular: am/is/are (present), was/were (past), been (past participle), being (present participle). Only a correctly conjugated finite form can serve as the main verb of a clause.

• Common SSC error: leaving the bare infinitive "be" where a finite verb (is/am/are/was/were) is required.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.
In industries, it is very common to observe that people show undue favour to one’s own relative during the hiring process.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. nepotism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nepotism" means the practice among people with power or influence of favouring their own relatives or friends, especially by giving them jobs. (भाई-भतीजावाद)
◦ Example: The company was criticised for nepotism after the manager hired his own nephew over more qualified candidates.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: racism — prejudice or discrimination against people based on their race; unrelated to favouring relatives.

• Option 3: liberalism — a political/social philosophy that emphasises individual rights and freedoms; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: communism — a political and economic ideology advocating collective ownership of property; unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• A related one-word substitute: "favouritism" (showing unfair preference to one person or group over others, not necessarily relatives) and "cronyism" (favouring close friends/associates, especially in appointments to positions, regardless of qualification).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Roshan, it’s time for you to give your speech to the whole school, wishing you luck to do well.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. break a leg.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Break a leg" is an informal expression used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance or an important task. (शुभकामनाएं / गुड लक)
◦ Example: You have your speech in five minutes — break a leg!

• The phrase is believed to have originated in theatre, where wishing someone "good luck" directly was considered to bring bad luck, so an ironic alternative was used instead.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: down in the dumps — means to feel sad or depressed; unrelated to wishing luck.

• Option 3: high five — a gesture of celebration or greeting where two people slap raised palms together; not used to wish luck.

• Option 4: hands down — means "easily" or "without a doubt" (e.g., "she won hands down"); unrelated to wishing luck.

NOTE

• Other idioms of good luck/encouragement often tested in SSC: "fingers crossed" (hoping for a good outcome), "knock on wood" (said to avoid bad luck), "best of luck".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
It takes time to adapt to a new environment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Adjust.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Adapt" means to become adjusted to new conditions; to change one’s behaviour to cope better with a new situation. (अनुकूल बनाना / समायोजित करना)

• "Adjust" means to alter or move something to fit a new situation or requirement, which closely matches the meaning of "adapt" in this context.
◦ Example: It took him a few weeks to adjust to the new environment after moving to a different city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Apply (आवेदन करना/लागू करना): To make a formal request or to put something into operation; it does not carry the sense of adjusting oneself to new conditions.

• Option 3: Understand (समझना): To comprehend something mentally; it does not involve behavioural change or adjustment.

• Option 4: Control (नियंत्रण करना): To have power over something; unrelated to the sense of adapting to surroundings.

NOTE

• Related words: adaptation, adaptable, adaptive — all connected to the idea of adjusting to change.

• Other synonyms of "adapt": acclimatise, accommodate, conform.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
One who tends to look at the dark side of things
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pessimist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pessimist" means a person who tends to see the worst aspect of things or believes that the worst will happen; one who takes a gloomy view of situations. (निराशावादी)
◦ Example: Being a pessimist, he always expected the project to fail even before it began.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Dynamist — one who believes in or advocates dynamism/constant activity and change; unrelated to a negative outlook.

• Option 2: Polemist (polemicist) — a person who engages in argument or controversy, especially about doctrine; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 3: Optimist — a person who tends to see the best/bright side of things; this is the direct opposite of the required word.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: "Cynic" (a person who believes people are motivated only by self-interest), "Fatalist" (one who believes all events are predetermined and cannot be changed).

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Recently, the (1)________ of heart-attacks in young Indians (2)________ increased tremendously. Doctors are surprised to note that young men and women with seemingly healthy lifestyle are suffering deadly heart attacks. (3)________ diet and exercise play a (4)________ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor. The (5)________ urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians which may be a major factor behind the increased numbers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. number.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank refers to "the number of heart-attacks", i.e., a count of how many heart-attacks are occurring — a countable quantity.

• Rule — Number vs Amount: "Number" is used with countable nouns (e.g., number of attacks, number of people), while "amount" is used with uncountable nouns (e.g., amount of water, amount of stress).

• Since "heart-attacks" is a countable noun (it has a plural form), the correct word to use is "number", giving: "the number of heart-attacks... increased tremendously."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: amount is incorrect because "amount" is used with uncountable nouns, not with a countable noun like "heart-attacks".

• Option 3: percent is incorrect because no percentage figure is being discussed in the passage; "percent" is not the required countable-quantity word.

• Option 4: height is incorrect because "height" refers to physical or metaphorical elevation/extent (e.g., "the height of the building" or "the height of the crisis"), not to a countable quantity of occurrences.

NOTE

• Other countable/uncountable pairs commonly tested in SSC cloze passages: many/much, few/little, number of/amount of, count/quantity.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Recently, the (1)________ of heart-attacks in young Indians (2)________ increased tremendously. Doctors are surprised to note that young men and women with seemingly healthy lifestyle are suffering deadly heart attacks. (3)________ diet and exercise play a (4)________ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor. The (5)________ urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians which may be a major factor behind the increased numbers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. has.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the verb is "the number of heart-attacks", which, despite containing a plural noun "heart-attacks", is treated as a singular subject because the head noun is "number" (as in "the number of... has/is").

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: With the phrase "the number of + plural noun" as subject, the verb must be singular — "The number of students has increased" (compare with "A number of students have arrived," where "a number of" takes a plural verb).

• Applying the rule: "the number of heart-attacks... has increased" is the grammatically correct present perfect form.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: have been is incorrect because it does not agree with the singular subject "the number", and "increased" would not correctly follow "have been" in this active sense (it would suggest a passive/continuous sense inappropriate here).

• Option 2: had is incorrect because the Past Perfect tense is not supported by the context, which describes a recent and ongoing trend ("Recently... increased tremendously"), not an action completed before another past action.

• Option 4: have is incorrect because it does not agree with the singular subject "the number of heart-attacks".

NOTE

• Distinguish carefully: "The number of + plural noun" → singular verb, but "A number of + plural noun" → plural verb. This distinction is a very frequently tested SSC grammar rule.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Recently, the (1)________ of heart-attacks in young Indians (2)________ increased tremendously. Doctors are surprised to note that young men and women with seemingly healthy lifestyle are suffering deadly heart attacks. (3)________ diet and exercise play a (4)________ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor. The (5)________ urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians which may be a major factor behind the increased numbers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Although.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence structure is: **"___ diet and exercise play a ___ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor."** This requires a connector that shows a contrast/concession between two clauses — the first stating that diet and exercise matter, and the second adding that mental health matters too.

• Rule — Subordinating Conjunctions of Concession: Words like "Although", "though", "even though" are used to join a subordinate clause to a main clause, showing that the main clause’s statement holds true despite what the subordinate clause says. They can appear at the start of a sentence and do not require "but" in the main clause.

• Applying the rule: "Although diet and exercise play a monumental role..., mental health is also a valuable factor" correctly connects the two ideas, showing that mental health matters in addition to diet and exercise.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Since is incorrect because "since" indicates a reason or a starting point in time, neither of which fits the contrast intended here.

• Option 3: In spite of is incorrect because "in spite of" is a preposition and must be followed by a noun/gerund (e.g., "in spite of playing"), not by a full clause with a finite verb ("diet and exercise play"); using it here would create a grammatically incomplete structure.

• Option 4: However is incorrect because "however" is a conjunctive adverb that typically starts a new independent sentence (often after a semicolon or full stop) rather than joining two clauses within one sentence as a subordinating conjunction.

NOTE

• Common confusion pair: "Although/though" (subordinating conjunction + clause) vs "In spite of/despite" (preposition + noun/gerund). Both express contrast but require different grammatical structures following them.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Recently, the (1)________ of heart-attacks in young Indians (2)________ increased tremendously. Doctors are surprised to note that young men and women with seemingly healthy lifestyle are suffering deadly heart attacks. (3)________ diet and exercise play a (4)________ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor. The (5)________ urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians which may be a major factor behind the increased numbers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. monumental.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank describes the role that diet and exercise play in a person’s overall wellbeing — the passage emphasises that this role is very significant/huge.

• "Monumental" means great in importance, extent, or size, and is commonly used with the word "role" to emphasise its significance (e.g., "played a monumental role").

• Applying this: "diet and exercise play a monumental role in a person’s overall wellbeing" conveys that diet and exercise are hugely important to wellbeing, which fits logically with the following clause about mental health also mattering.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: historic is incorrect because it means "important in history" or "famous in the past", which does not fit describing the general significance of diet and exercise on wellbeing.

• Option 2: epic is incorrect because it means "grand in scale, like an epic poem/story" — it does not naturally collocate with "role" in the sense of importance here.

• Option 4: increased is incorrect because it is used to describe change over time ("an increased role"), not the sheer scale/importance meant here, and it also creates redundancy with "increased" used earlier and later in the passage.

NOTE

• Common collocations with "role": play a vital/crucial/pivotal/significant/monumental role. These words are frequently tested as synonym-fit options in SSC cloze passages.

(3)________ diet and exercise play a (4)________ role in a person’s overall wellbeing, mental health is also a valuable factor. The (5)________ urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians which may be a major factor behind the increased numbers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. fast-paced.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank describes the type of "urban lifestyle" that is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians — the passage implies a lifestyle that is hectic and rushed.

• "Fast-paced" means characterised by rapid activity or development; hectic, which fits naturally as an adjective describing "urban lifestyle" and logically explains why it causes anxiety and depression.

• Applying this: "The fast-paced urban lifestyle is causing anxiety and depression in young Indians" makes clear, logical sense in context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: cosmic is incorrect because it means "relating to the universe" and does not describe a lifestyle in a meaningful way here.

• Option 3: rapidly is incorrect because it is an adverb, not an adjective, and grammatically cannot modify the noun "urban lifestyle" directly (the blank needs an adjective before the noun).

• Option 4: wilderness is incorrect because it is a noun meaning "an uncultivated, uninhabited region", which cannot function as an adjective modifying "urban lifestyle", and is also contextually opposite to an urban setting.

NOTE

• Word-form errors (using a noun/adverb where an adjective is needed, or vice versa) are common wrong-option traps in SSC cloze passages — always check what part of speech the blank grammatically requires.
